knowledge_point.title: Recognizing Parts of the Invertible Matrix Theorem

question.:question/problem:
$$
\begin{gathered}A\text{ is }\text{invertible} \\ \Updownarrow \\ \left\{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Col}(A) &=\mathbb{R}^{n} \\ \dim(\operatorname{Col}(A)) &=n=\operatorname{rank}(A) \\ \operatorname{Null}(A) &=\{0\} \\ \dim(\operatorname{Null}(A)) &=0=\underline{\phantom{WWWW}}\end{aligned}\right.\end{gathered}
$$

Consider the equivalence above, where $A$ is a real $n\times n$ matrix and $n$ is a positive integer. Which of the following should be placed into the blank space to make a true statement?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the *invertible matrix theorem* states the following:

*Let $A$ be a real $n\times n$ matrix. Then we have the following equivalence:*

$$
\begin{gathered}A\text{ is }\text{invertible} \\ \Updownarrow \\ \left\{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Col}(A) &=\mathbb{R}^{n} \\ \dim(\operatorname{Col}(A)) &=n=\operatorname{rank}(A) \\ \operatorname{Null}(A) &=\{0\} \\ \dim(\operatorname{Null}(A)) &=0=\operatorname{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}\right.\end{gathered}
$$

Therefore, the missing expression is $\operatorname{nullity}(A)$.

generation.domain: real n by n matrix; integer n >= 1
